title: bug: the daemon records a relative --project or MOE_PROJECT_PATH (the README's terminal-only `moe-daemon init --project .`) verbatim as daemon.json projectPath, /health projectPath and project.json rootPath, so a later start from another folder and the JetBrains plugin both read the live daemon as another project, delete its daemon.json and start a second daemon on the same .moe/
description:
Filed by defect hunt task-3488566e (11-04 #17, lane 2: the JetBrains plugin's daemon spawn/reuse, root cause on the daemon side). HEAD bb0bc17e.

PROBLEM
- packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts:67 keeps --project, or MOE_PROJECT_PATH, exactly as typed. :844-850 writes it into daemon.json, /health reports it, and normalizeProject (state/persistence.ts:97, applied at StateManager.ts:1058-1062 on every load) rewrites project.json rootPath to it. index.ts:94-95 already notes that "the daemon records `--project` as given".
- README.md:112 tells terminal-only users to run `moe-daemon init --project .`. The daemon then records projectPath "." and rootPath ".".
- "." names a different directory for every later reader whose cwd differs:
  - The daemon's own start guard (existingDaemonBlocksStart, index.ts:619-625, through validateDaemonInfoForProject/namesOwnProject) run from another folder judges the live daemon stale, logs "Cleaning up stale daemon lifecycle files" and starts a second daemon. The first daemon released its lock once daemon.json was written (index.ts:859), so nothing stops the second one.
  - JetBrains MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:151-166: isSameProject(".", base) (:970-972; DaemonIdentity.kt:96 collapses "." to "", and File(".").canonicalPath is the IDE's cwd) is false. The plugin skips reuse, deletes the live daemon's daemon.json and spawns its own (:180-203) on project open, reconnect or Restart Daemon.
  - Both plugins compare the STATE_SNAPSHOT rootPath and disconnect on "." (MoeMessageDispatcher.kt:93-98; moe-vscode MoeDaemonClient.ts:1860-1863).
- The result is two daemons writing one .moe/, which breaks the sole-writer invariant. The agent launchers pass an absolute project, so seats alone never trigger it.

EVIDENCE
- Architect re-run on the bb0bc17e snapshot (ports 19886/19887, isolated HOME): /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-3488566e/mine/relative-project-guard-rerun.txt
  live daemon pid=2052204 projectPath=. port=19886; project.json rootPath=.
  (start --project <abs> run from cwd /) WARN: Cleaning up stale daemon lifecycle files ... INFO: Moe daemon running
  daemon.json now: pid 2052253 port 19887 projectPath /tmp/hunt-3488-snap/fixtures/relproj-mine; first pid 2052204 alive: yes
- JetBrains path (Kotlin logic mirrored, no Gradle run): /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-3488566e/A/repro-relative-project.sh and .out, plus kotlin-isSameProject-mirror.mjs.
  isSameProject(".", "/tmp/hunt-3488-A/fixtures/relproj") = false
  daemon.json now: {"port": 19877, "pid": 1937315, ..., "projectPath": "/tmp/hunt-3488-A/fixtures/relproj"}
  first daemon _run pid 1937243 alive: yes; /health on 19876 still: 200

FIX DIRECTION
- In parseArgs (index.ts:59-72), resolve a relative --project or MOE_PROJECT_PATH to an absolute path once, before anything records or compares it.
- Leave POSIX-absolute, drive-letter and UNC values unchanged. moe-proxy/src/utils.ts:39 uses the same rule: `WINDOWS_FORM.test(raw) || raw.startsWith('/') ? raw : path.resolve(raw)`.
- normalizeProject rewrites rootPath from the daemon's project path at every load, so an existing project.json whose rootPath is "." heals at its next start. No client change is needed.
- Out of scope: the JetBrains bindHost probe (a sibling row filed by the same hunt), Kotlin code, the README, docs/MCP_SERVER.md.

FILES: packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts, packages/moe-daemon/src/index.test.ts (or a new src/index.relativeProject.test.ts). No open row holds either (lanes.js 06:50Z). The same hunt held back a doctor row (WSL-foreign daemon.json) that wants to move isForeignDaemonInfo/wslGatewayHost out of index.ts; it waits for this row to land.
definitionOfDone: A vitest starts the daemon CLI with `init --project .` from a temp cwd, and once more with MOE_PROJECT_PATH=. and no --project. It asserts that daemon.json projectPath, the /health projectPath and project.json rootPath each equal path.resolve(cwd).

A vitest proves that a second `start --project <absolute path>` run from another cwd while that daemon lives logs 'Moe daemon already running', leaves daemon.json's pid unchanged and starts no second daemon (the case /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-3488566e/A/repro-relative-daemon-guard.sh drives). Absolute POSIX, drive-letter and UNC --project values are recorded unchanged.
`npx vitest run src/index.test.ts` (plus any new test file) passes in a snapshot outside the shared checkout, with the run's output as the completion evidence.
